subsystems.name: Cell source and expansion
subsystems.role: provides the living building blocks — typically induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) or adult stem cells.

subsystems.name: Bio-ink
subsystems.role: a printable mixture of cells, nutrients and a gel-like matrix that holds them in place.

subsystems.name: Bioprinter
subsystems.role: deposits the bio-ink layer by layer into a defined 3D shape.

subsystems.name: Scaffold or support structure
subsystems.role: gives the printed cells a temporary shape until they self-organise.

subsystems.name: Maturation and incubation
subsystems.role: lets the printed cells multiply, differentiate and fold into organ-like structures.

subsystems.name: Quality control and screening
subsystems.role: checks that the organoids are healthy and measures their response to drugs.

buildSteps.title: Expand stem cells
buildSteps.detail: iPSCs or adult stem cells are thawed and grown in large quantities under controlled conditions, then harvested and counted.

buildSteps.title: Formulate bio-ink
buildSteps.detail: Cells are mixed with a hydrogel precursor, nutrients and growth factors at a density of millions of cells per millilitre, kept cool to preserve viability.

buildSteps.title: Design the print layout
buildSteps.detail: Software converts an organoid model — for example a 0.5 mm-wide liver lobule — into a toolpath that fits a standard 96- or 384-well plate.

buildSteps.title: Print the structure
buildSteps.detail: The bioprinter extrudes the bio-ink through a nozzle (often 100–400 µm wide) in successive layers, sometimes alongside a sacrificial support gel.

buildSteps.title: Crosslink or solidify
buildSteps.detail: The printed gel is set by brief UV light, a chemical crosslinker or a temperature shift so the shape holds.

buildSteps.title: Incubate to self-organise
buildSteps.detail: The printed constructs are placed in an incubator or perfusion bioreactor for days to weeks; cells rearrange and differentiate into organoid-like tissues.

buildSteps.title: Validate the organoids
buildSteps.detail: Microscopy, gene expression and functional tests (e.g. albumin secretion for liver organoids) confirm the structures behave like real tissue.

buildSteps.title: Run drug screens
buildSteps.detail: Compounds are added automatically; imaging and metabolic assays measure toxicity or efficacy across many organoids at once.

pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper safety screening of drug candidates before animal trials.
